name: headsup-mcp

tools.name: notify_user
tools.description:
Play a short spoken alert on the user's computer speakers so they can come back to it. Call it once at the end of a turn (or when starting something long), picking the status that matches why you stopped:
- completed: the task is done ("I've completed the task.")
- review: work is ready for the user to review (diff, design, document) ("I need your review.")
- feedback: you want the user's opinion on a draft or direction ("I need your feedback.")
- input: you need information or a decision from the user ("I need your input.")
- approval: you are waiting on a permission prompt or go-ahead ("I need your approval to continue.")
- question: you have a short clarifying question ("I have a quick question for you.")
- blocked: you cannot make progress without the user ("I'm stuck, and I need your help.")
- error: an unexpected error or crash needs the user's attention ("Something went wrong. Please take a look.")
- tests_passed: a test run finished green ("All the tests are passing.")
- tests_failed: a test run finished with failures you could not fix ("Some tests are failing.")
- deployed: a deploy or release succeeded ("The deployment is live.")
- deploy_failed: a deploy or release failed ("The deployment failed.")
- pr_ready: a PR is open and ready for the user ("The pull request is ready.")
- next_task: you are idle and waiting for new work ("I'm ready for the next task.")
- limit_warning: usage or quota is nearly used up ("I'm close to my usage limit.")
- limit_reached: usage or quota is used up and work stopped ("I've hit my usage limit.")
- sign_in: a login, OAuth or credential step needs the user ("I need you to sign in.")
- long_task: you are starting something long and the user can step away ("This will take a while. I'll let you know when it's done.")
- progress: a long task is still running ("Quick update. I'm still working on it.")
- reminder: you asked for something earlier and are still waiting ("I'm still waiting on you.")
Their settings (off switch, mute, quiet hours, location lock, cooldown) may block it; a skipped alert is not an error, so don't retry.

repeat.description: How many times to play the line (use 2 for something urgent).

message.description: Optional: your own line, spoken instead of the status's fixed line when that line doesn't say enough (e.g. "The migration ran, but two tables need your review. Should I roll back or keep going?"). Plain sentences in first person, at most 160 characters (the user's setting): use that room to say exactly what you need, such as which review, which decision and its options, or which input. No code, paths, links or secrets, because it may go to the user's text-to-speech provider. Still pick the closest status: if the line can't be recorded, the status's line plays instead.

folder.description: The absolute path of the folder this work happened in. Pass it whenever that isn't the folder the session started in (you changed into another repo, or work in a subfolder of a parent like ~/Dev), so the greeting names the right project. It's only used to look up the project's name.

volume.description: Optional target volume %. Leave it out: volume is handled automatically within their safety caps.
